title: Research: per-helper-sector census of the literal K_equals_D defect on retained R439 helper-star words (no new kappa)
body:
## Summary

Adds `research/r439-star-kdefect-sectors/`: a complete per-helper-sector census of the syntactic `K_equals_D` failure carried by the three retained R439 helper-star words (seed19 candidate from the PR967 lineage; PR1062 `composition` and `candidate`), under the pinned owner checker's own definitions (`research/e8-bit-p111-tuned/code/xcheck_p.py`).

Established (finite certificate on three named words at base `bb4bccbf42844d2801487450727c2f63e10d1d0f`):

| word | D gates | defect bits (K ⊕ N) | defective helper sectors | sector-local KS(h) pass | single-gate repairs | single-bit repair |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| seed19 candidate | 1,165 | 17,636 | 439 / 439 | 0 / 439 | 0 | no |
| PR1062 composition | 1,165 | 17,636 | 439 / 439 | 0 / 439 | 0 | no |
| PR1062 candidate | 1,195 | 17,653 | 439 / 439 | 0 / 439 | 0 | no |

- **Global, not local:** all 439 helper sectors are defective (sector sizes 4–68 targets); a per-helper sector-local replacement of H2/K cannot lift to the global flag — any replacement must carry cross-sector hypotheses, consistent with the retained global PR1194 route.
- **No single-operation repair:** exhaustive enumeration of all single-D-gate removals and all single-bit toggles yields zero repairs on every word.
- **Localization:** the raw helper part K is bit-identical across all three words (0 differing bits) although phase-B replacement rewrites B (712→578) and C (2,574→2,440); identical D leaves the defect exactly at 17,636 bits; the star rerun (+30 D gates, N differing in 173 bits) moves the defect by 17 bits. The failure lives entirely in D versus the fixed raw helper component.
- **H2 clause split:** frame clauses are clean on all words (0 nonzero-frame gates, 0 start violations); H2 fails purely via destination/read clauses (442/442/472 non-target-writing and 612 non-helper-reading D gates).

An independent GF(2) all-column replay agrees with the pinned owner checker on `K_equals_D`, `J_identity` and `U_block_form` for all three words, and full exact-legality replay passes as a positive control (the words are legal while carrying the quantified failure).

## Related open work

- #3533 — abstract three-gate restored-edge K-mask mechanism; this PR counts that mechanism's consequence across full retained words (no numerical conflict; different object scale).
- #3904 — pins one **D-inclusive** per-target example (target 112, helper column 260). Checked numerically against this census: under the checker's official raw definition `W0 = (A, scatter, B)` (D excluded), used here, that bit pair is not in the defect set (column 260's sector has 57 defective targets, not including 112). Different raw-word definitions; no contradiction, and the distinction is documented in the package README.
- #3891 — prices a helper-star interface word; addresses the paid-profile side, not the syntactic K failure decomposition; no overlapping number.

## Validation

- `python3 -I -B research/r439-star-kdefect-sectors/verify.py` and the `-O` variant: `PASS_R439_STAR_KDEFECT_SECTORS words=3 defect_bits=17636/17636/17653 defective_sectors=439/439/439 KS_pass=0/439/0/439/0/439 single_op_repairs=0 controls=5 no_new_kappa` (~2 s each, standard library, CPython 3.12.15).
- `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-star-kdefect-sectors`: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE outcome=completed`.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/r439-star-kdefect-sectors --check-source-history`: `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Scope and limits

Finite certificate on three named words; not a proof that every weakened per-operation contract fails (a changed contract with named cross-sector hypotheses escapes it); no supplier admission; no κ, paid-profile or selected-frontier change; no native, hosted, all-size or cold-replay execution (not requested by this package). Inputs bound by SHA-256 in `SOURCES.json`.

Prepared by Nick Petalas with AI assistance.
